newsitem.title: USA: Court denies SEC plea for viatical case rehearing.
newsitem.headline: Court denies SEC plea for viatical case rehearing.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday its petition was denied for a rehearing of an appeals court panel ruling favoring a Texas firm selling interests from insurance policies of AIDS victims.
The order denying the petition was issued by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, the agency said. The SEC had filed the rehearing request in August.
A three judge panel of the court had previously ruled against the SEC and in favor of Life Partners Inc, a Waco-Texas firm that is in the "viatical" business.
The firm, the biggest player in the viatical industry, sells portions of the life insurance policies of AIDS patients at a discount.
The SEC contends that the insurance policy interests the firm sells are "securities" and therefore must register those securities with the agency.

A three-member panel of the appeals court ruled in July against the SEC. That ruling overturned a district court decision earlier this year ordering Life Partners not to resume selling until it complied with SEC requiremtns.
Ross Albert, an SEC lawyer, said, "We are still analyzing the decision and considering all of our options."
Those options include elavating the case to the Supreme Court. She said the SEC has 90 days within which to decide what steps it should take.
